Subject: Post-demo: retrieval probe set & ranking strategy for Avalon Health

Thanks again for the demo time today — great conversation. Per our call, I wanted to capture the concrete next steps and give an initial recommendation for the RAG evaluation we discussed so your engineering team can kick off a quick internal POC.

High-level ask from you: get us a representative set of questions and a small corpus snapshot (1–2k docs) so we can run a focused probe to validate grounding and hallucination risk. Below are the items we can action immediately.

What we will deliver (initial):
- A probe set (attached: avalon_probe_set_v1.csv) derived from the use cases you described (clinical note summarization, clinician Q&A, billing policy lookup).
- An evaluation notebook with metrics and example failures (attached: avalon_rag_eval_notebook.ipynb).
- Two recommended model+retrieval configurations to try (fast vs. high-precision).

Initial retrieval + reranker recommendations (short):
- Retriever: hybrid BM25 + semantic (embedding) with hybrid weight 0.25 BM25 / 0.75 semantic; chunk size 800 chars with 50% overlap; top_k retrieval = 100.
- Reranker: cross-encoder reranker for the precision pass (we recommend fine-tuning a cross-encoder on 1k labeled pairs). Fallback: bi-encoder candidate ranking with a lightweight MLP.

Model recommendations for the first-run POC:
- Redwood-optimized Llama-3-13B-int8 (balanced latency/cost) — target for production latency SLOs.
- Lightweight baseline: open-3.7B-quant for speed checks and cost sensitivity.

Key metrics we'll measure in the probe run:
- Grounding precision (fraction of answers backed by retrieved doc spans).
- Hallucination rate (manual label + automated heuristics).
- Latency per request (p50/p95) and token cost estimates.

Requested action items for your team:
1) Share a 1–2k doc snapshot (s3 link or uploaded to shared Drive).
2) Send 100–200 representative user questions (we included a starter probe set in the attachment).
3) Give us 2–3 examples of safety/PII redaction rules we should enforce when grounding.

Timing: we can run the initial probe within 3 business days after we receive the artifacts above; summary results + playbook in 5 business days.

Attaching: avalon_probe_set_v1.csv (starter probe), eval notebook, and a short PDF comparing reranker trade-offs.

Open to a quick 30-minute follow-up if you want a walkthrough of the probe set.

Thanks,

Thanks — quick answers below and a slightly more detailed plan for the probe run.

1) Hybrid weight rationale: 0.25 BM25 / 0.75 semantic is a starting heuristic we use for clinical text where semantic matches are important but keyword precision still helps with short policy lookups. It comes from prior Avalon-like customers where initial runs showed better grounding recall with semantic emphasis. We'll tune it during the probe and surface a per-query weight if there are strong differences by intent.

2) Cross-encoder hosting: for the probe you can run the cross-encoder on Redwood Hosted (faster to spin up) — Dedicated is recommended once you have production throughput requirements and want predictable latency/SLA. For the probe, Hosted + small batch size (8) will be fine.

Probe run configuration (what we'll execute once we have artifacts):
- Preprocessing: chunk docs at 800 chars, 50% overlap, canonicalize abbreviations per your examples.
- Retriever phase: BM25 + semantic hybrid scoring, embeddings = redwood-embed-1-large (or text-embedding-3-large as fallback).
- Candidate pool: top_k = 100; rerank top 20 with cross-encoder for final answer selection.
- Metrics: grounding precision (automated span match), top-1 evidence coverage, automated hallucination heuristics + 50 manual labels sampled for precision.

Prompting + prompt set: we attached a starter prompt_set_avalon_v1.txt in the Drive link. For stability we'll run 6 prompt variants across templates: conservative-grounded, evidence-first, short-answer, clinician-style summary, cite-and-explain, and follow-up-clarifying.

I'll loop Rishi on details around reranker trade-offs — see his note below.

Best,
Mina

Quick reranker note (trade-offs + recommendation):

Why use a cross-encoder?
- Pros: best precision on short evidence selection tasks, reduces hallucinations where evidence spans are subtle.
- Cons: higher CPU/GPU cost and increased latency (especially if reranking many candidates).

Practical suggestion for the probe:
- Keep candidate pool at 100 but only cross-encode top 20 — this gives most of the precision benefits while bounding cost.
- If latency is a hard constraint, use a two-stage hybrid: bi-encoder scoring for top 50, cheap learned rerank (MLP) for top 20, cross-encoder only on a sampled 10% of requests for deeper analysis.
- Evaluate two rerank models in parallel for 48 hours: (A) cross-encoder tuned on your labeled pairs, (B) bi-encoder + small MLP trained on synthetic negatives from your corpus. We'll compare grounding precision and p95 latency.

Operational notes:
- For the cross-encoder probe we recommend Hosted Dedicated G5s (or equivalent) if you need sub-400ms p95; otherwise expect 600–900ms p95 on smaller instances.
- We'll produce a cost/latency and grounding trade-off chart in the eval notebook.

I'll add the reranker comparison PDF to the Drive folder and flag the sections to look at for productionization.
